title: tea README links point at /docs, which moved to packages/tea/docs
rawReport:
## Summary
Eight links in the tea README return 404 on GitHub. They point at `blob/main/docs/...`, but the docs have lived under `packages/tea/docs/` since the monorepo move. The README is what npm shows, so this is the first thing a new consumer clicks.

## What I was doing
A docs sweep of `packages/tea`, started because the "on the Effect engine" link in the README was reported dead.

## What I observed
`packages/tea/README.md` lines 62, 63, 65, 70, 72, 73, 74 and 75 all use the prefix `https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/blob/main/docs/`. None of those paths exist. The same files exist under `packages/tea/docs/`:

- `how-to/run-on-the-promise-engine.md` (line 62)
- `how-to/run-on-the-effect-engine.md` (line 63)
- `how-to/migrate-from-0-15.md` (line 65)
- `README.md` (line 70)
- `tutorial/index.md`, `how-to/index.md`, `reference/index.md`, `explanation/index.md` (lines 72 to 75)

The `.patterns/` and `.decisions/` links on lines 78 and 79 are fine, because those folders are at the repo root.

A script that resolved every markdown link in `packages/tea/README.md`, `packages/tea/MAINTAINING.md` and the 62 files under `packages/tea/docs/` found these 8 and no others. The README was last touched after the move (commit `8883e16`, "monorepo — tea to packages/tea"), and the links were not updated then.

`.github/workflows/build.yaml` has no step that checks doc links, so nothing caught it.

## Why it matters
Every docs entry point from the npm page is dead. A reader who lands on the package cannot reach the tutorials, the how-tos, the reference or the migration guide without guessing the path.

## Pointers
- `packages/tea/README.md:62-75`
- `packages/tea/docs/` (where the targets are)
- `.github/workflows/build.yaml` (no link check)
- `packages/tea/src/docs/doc-specifiers.test.ts` (an existing test that reads the doc pages; a link check could sit next to it)

## Suggested next step (non-binding)
Change the prefix on those 8 links to `blob/main/packages/tea/docs/`. A small test that resolves README and docs links against the file tree would stop it from coming back.

---

enriched:
## In plain words

Eight links in the tea README lead to a "page not found" on GitHub. The README is what npm shows, so a new user cannot click through to the tutorials, how-tos, reference or migration guide. We fix the eight links and teach the existing link test to check this kind of link, so it does not come back.

## What is wrong

`packages/tea/README.md` lines 62, 63, 65, 70, 72, 73, 74 and 75 link to `https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/blob/main/docs/...`. There is no `docs/` folder at the repo root. The targets live under `packages/tea/docs/`:

| Line | Target under `packages/tea/docs/` |
|---|---|
| 62 | `how-to/run-on-the-promise-engine.md` |
| 63 | `how-to/run-on-the-effect-engine.md` |
| 65 | `how-to/migrate-from-0-15.md` |
| 70 | `README.md` |
| 72 | `tutorial/index.md` |
| 73 | `how-to/index.md` |
| 74 | `reference/index.md` |
| 75 | `explanation/index.md` |

Lines 78 and 79 (`.patterns/index.md`, `.decisions/index.md`) use the same URL form and are correct, because those folders are at the repo root.

## Why nothing caught it

Triage note: the original report says no test checks doc links. That is half right. A link gate already exists at `packages/tea/src/docs/doc-links.ts` with `doc-links.test.ts`, and it reads `README.md`, `MAINTAINING.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and every page under `packages/tea/docs/`. It only checks relative links. `filePathOf` returns `undefined` for any target with a scheme (`https:`), so these eight absolute GitHub URLs were skipped. So the fix for "stop it coming back" is to widen that gate, not to add a second one.

Triage note: read at `origin/main` (`d8b76de`). All eight links are still dead there, and all eight target files exist under `packages/tea/docs/`.

## The fix

1. In `packages/tea/README.md`, change the prefix on those eight links from `blob/main/docs/` to `blob/main/packages/tea/docs/`. Keep them absolute: `packages/tea/package.json` publishes `dist` only, so the docs are not in the npm tarball and the README has to point at GitHub.
2. In `packages/tea/src/docs/doc-links.ts`, treat a link to this repo's own tree (`https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/blob/main/<path>` and the `tree/main` form) as a file path resolved from the repo root, and report it when the file is missing. Every other external URL stays out of scope, as today.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The eight links on lines 62, 63, 65, 70, 72, 73, 74 and 75 of `packages/tea/README.md` point at `https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/blob/main/packages/tea/docs/...` and each names a file that exists in the tree.
- [ ] The link gate in `packages/tea/src/docs/doc-links.ts` resolves a `https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/blob/main/<path>` link against the repo root and reports it when `<path>` does not exist.
- [ ] A test in `packages/tea/src/docs/doc-links.test.ts` feeds the pure core a `blob/main/docs/how-to/x.md` link that names a missing file and asserts a hit, and feeds it one that resolves and asserts none.
- [ ] Links to other hosts and other repos are still ignored by the gate.
- [ ] The gate passes over the committed tree, including the `.patterns/` and `.decisions/` links on README lines 78 and 79.
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` pass from the root.

### No-gos

- Do not rewrite README prose beyond the eight link targets.
- Do not make the gate fetch anything over the network.
- The other doc findings from the same sweep are #538 and stay there.

## Triage notes

- Triage note: minted standalone. Searched the board for "tea README links 404 docs moved" and "doc link check README dead links". The only docs ticket is #538, the wider docs sweep from the same session, which says these eight links are filed on their own and is not yet triaged. #356, which added the relative-link gate, is closed.
- Triage note: judged visible to a signed-out visitor. The README renders on the public npm page and on GitHub, and the dead links are its only way into the docs. That sets the floor at `p1`.
- Triage note: npm shows the README from the last published version, so the npm page keeps the dead links until the next `@demlik/tea` release. Whether this change needs its own changeset is not settled here.
